revision: 2026-08-16 — redone under the revised METHODOLOGY.md §6 (a)-(e) (failure-path file/type renames + failure-path log-statement rewrites + log regenerated from the anonymized source). Supersedes the 2026-08-11 minimal version.
policy: Case-targeted, not system-hiding. The failure path here is a single file: it holds the root-causing line and every frame of the symptom stack trace. That file's name, its public type, and all of its log printing statements are anonymized; everything else stays real — package paths, the ZooKeeper / ClientCnxn / KeeperException / Stat classes and their bodies, znode/session/quorum vocabulary, the entire server-side log, and ClientCnxn's per-request DEBUG telemetry.

failure_path.definition_used: files named in the fix diff + files named in the symptom-log stack trace
failure_path.note: private/fix.diff touches only ZooKeeperMain.java (plus CHANGES.txt and a test), and all six stack frames are in that same file.

bug_id_scrub.note: Neither the reporting ticket nor the trunk ticket carrying the fix may appear in any LLM-facing artifact. The scratch clone path and reproduce.sh's temp dir were moved to neutral paths (repos/zookeeper-anonymized, /tmp/zk-repro-XXXX) because the JVM prints java.class.path and user.dir into the log.

distinctive_term_renames.where: commandMap.put("stat","path [watch]") and the dispatch branch cmd.equals("stat"); consequently every prompt line and the LOG.debug dispatch line in the log
distinctive_term_renames.why: the term that names the case — the ticket is literally 'stat command on non-existing node causes NPE'

distinctive_term_renames.where: the failure-path file; consequently the top frame of the stack trace in the log
distinctive_term_renames.why: the distinctive token of the stack trace the JIRA report quotes verbatim

references_updated: the logger name, so log4j's %C{1} tag prints CliShellMain
the inner class in ZooKeeper.java's connection log line (watcher=org.apache.zookeeper.CliShellMain$MyWatcher@…)
all six frames of the stack trace in logs/symptom.log (regenerated, not rewritten)
failure_path_file_type_renames.why: blocks 'I recognize org.apache.zookeeper.ZooKeeperMain.printStat → this is the known zkCli stat NPE ticket' mapping from parametric memory

failure_path_log_statement_rewrites.scope: every string literal printed by the failure-path file (shell prompt, banner/connect lines, the LOG.debug dispatch line, the znode-metadata labels printed by printNodeMeta, and processCmd's catch-arm messages). Wording changes; the kind and quantity of information does not. Log statements in files that are NOT on the failure path (server side, ClientCnxn's per-request DEBUG telemetry) are left untouched so the log still reads as genuine system output.
failure_path_log_statement_rewrites.not_rewritten: KeeperException.java's javadoc comment '/** Node does not exist */' on the NONODE code — an API doc comment in a non-failure-path file, not a log printing statement.

jira_quoted_text.what_the_ticket_quotes: a 6-frame NullPointerException stack trace (printStat <- processZKCmd <- processCmd <- executeLine <- run <- main, ZooKeeperMain.java lines 130/722/581/353/311/270 in 3.3.5) and a transcript line '[zk: c0405(CONNECTED) 3] stat /foobar'
jira_quoted_text.how_handled: Not blanked (the trace is the observable symptom) but fully de-matched: every frame now reads org.apache.zookeeper.CliShellMain.<method>(CliShellMain.java:NN) with printNodeMeta on top, and the transcript line reads '[client: 127.0.0.1:21812(CONNECTED) 7] meta /app/workers/w4242'. No string in the ticket matches the log.

log_regeneration.how: copy the pre-fix tree (deps-fix applied) to repos/zookeeper-anonymized → rename file/type → rename distinctive terms → rewrite failure-path log literals → `ant jar` → re-run reproduce.sh (STAT_CMD=meta, MAIN_CLASS=org.apache.zookeeper.CliShellMain, NONODE_MSG='No such node:', PORT=21812) → publish logs/symptom.log + source/ → verify.
log_regeneration.guarantee: logs/symptom.log is the genuine 9,555-line DEBUG output of the anonymized binary (3,146 DEBUG lines); it is never a post-hoc rewrite of the M3 log, so its literals and stack frames match source/ exactly. The symptom still reproduces (client exit code 1, uncaught NPE, no graceful missing-node message).
